nodes.title: Zink coefficient ring
nodes.statement: For a complete Noetherian local ring R with perfect residue field k of characteristic p>2, use the canonical Frobenius-stable subring Ŵ(R) of W(R) whose reduction to W(k) is surjective and whose kernel consists of Witt coordinates tending to zero in the maximal-ideal topology. Its canonical additive splitting is W(k) ⊕ Ŵ(m_R); this does not assume a ring section k→R. Put Î_R=ker(w₀:Ŵ(R)→R). Frobenius and Verschiebung restrict and V:Ŵ(R)→Î_R is an additive bijection.
proofSteps: Construct first on Artin quotients, identify the decaying-coordinate kernel and pass to the inverse limit. Prove closure under Witt operations and compatibility with the canonical W(k) lift; use the restricted Witt identities, rather than coordinatewise multiplication.
acceptance: Prove the stated comparison with all displayed base rings and conventions; expose the actual maps, not only an existence proposition.

nodes.title: Display frame

nodes.title: Dieudonné modules over perfect rings
nodes.statement: For a perfect F_p-algebra R, contravariant Dieudonné theory is an anti-equivalence between p-divisible groups over Spec R and finite projective W(R)-modules M with σ-linear F and σ⁻¹-linear V satisfying FV=VF=p. Equivalently the linearization β:σ*M→M obeys pM⊂β(σ*M)⊂M and becomes an isomorphism after inverting p. Height is locally constant; do not impose a global basis or confuse perfect with a general reduced smooth base.
proofSteps: Lemma2.4 identifies the finite-projective Dieudonné and display categories over perfect rings; Gabber’s theorem gives the group. Apply Cartier duality for our convention. Prove local projectivity of the F/V quotients, rather than adding a freeness assumption.
acceptance: Recover the perfect-field base theorem, permit disconnected perfect rings of locally varying rank, and export the induced GL-shtuka β with its height-one bound.

nodes.title: Integral tensor and local-model datum
nodes.statement: Fix p>2, k=F̄_p, W=W(k), a finite free Z_p-module Λ, and a family s_a in the direct sum of mixed tensor powers of Λ and Λ∨. Require a smooth affine full fixer G̃⊂GL(Λ), with connected reductive generic fibre G, cut out scheme-theoretically by s_a on every Z_p-algebra. Write Gscr=G̃ for this full fixer and Gscr° for its connected parahoric subgroup. A good integral Hodge embedding includes scalars, a minuscule weight-(0,1) conjugacy class and a compatible closed immersion of its supplied flat normal local model into Gr(d,Λ). A point x and a tensor frame D(H₀)≅Λ_W complete the marked datum. For generic-fixer and cocharacter statements retain the full fixer even when Gscr°≠Gscr.
proofSteps: Use the scheme stabilizer rather than only its Z_p-points. Import the group scheme and local-model carriers; package their specified embedding as input. The missing existence/local-model supplier extension is recorded as a gap, so this definition does not assert that every parahoric datum has a good embedding.
acceptance: Prove the stated comparison with all displayed base rings and conventions; expose the actual maps, not only an existence proposition.

nodes.title: The crystalline Galois image has trivial Kottwitz invariant
nodes.statement: Let k be algebraically closed, K/W(k)[1/p] finite, and L a crystalline lattice with Γ_K-invariant tensors cutting out a smooth integral group Gscr with connected reductive generic G. nodes.title: Hyperspecial Breuil–Kisin tensor frames
nodes.statement: Let k be perfect, K/W(k)[1/p] finite totally ramified, and L a crystalline Z_p-lattice with invariant tensors cutting out a reductive group over Z_p. Their images cut out a reductive group on the imported module 𝔐(L) for every such k. A tensor-preserving frame L⊗𝔖≅𝔐(L) exists if k is separably closed, or if k is finite and the integral group is connected. nodes.title: Relative evaluation of the crystalline period construction
nodes.statement: Let R be a normal Noetherian integral p-adically complete p-torsion-free ring with R/p nonzero, in the relative comparison range of Kisin17 §1.1.15. In a chosen algebraic closure of Frac R take the directed union R̄ of its normalizations in finite extensions étale over R[1/p], and let R̂̄ be its p-adic completion. Apply CrystallineCohomology:CR.0/fontaine-envelope to R̂̄ to obtain θ and A_cris(R). The notation A_cris(R) here includes the chosen geometric cover; it does not construct a second PD envelope or assert its absolute perfect-field properties for arbitrary R.
proofSteps: Build the normal-cover system and its compatible Galois action, check the hypotheses making θ onto in this setting, and evaluate the existing Fontaine-envelope construction. All PD-envelope algebra remains with CR.0. The needed relative comparison is separately recorded as a gap.

nodes.statement: For a crystalline Γ_K-lattice L and invariant cutting tensors with smooth full fixer Gscr and connected reductive generic G, suppose the image lies in Gscr°(Z_p) and H¹(U,Gscr°)=1 for U=Spec𝔖\{(p,u)}. Then 𝔐(L) has an integral tensor-preserving frame L⊗𝔖≅𝔐(L). Modern parahoric purity supplies the vanishing for the connected parahoric in its coefficient-ring range; the tame/no-E₈ conditions of KP18 Corollary3.3.6 are a valid older sufficient case, not hypotheses silently needed in KZ25.
proofSteps: Apply the Dedekind-base integral Tannakian torsor theorem to the exact faithful tensor functor on U, using finite-rank stable pieces of the group coordinate algebra. Kill its connected-parahoric torsor by the stated H¹ vanishing, then extend the tensor frame through the puncture by Hartogs for finite free modules. Tannakian representability and purity remain separate supplier obligations.

nodes.title: Rational tensor torsor for conjugate admissible filtrations
nodes.statement: For a connected reductive Q_p-group G and a fixed crystalline G-isocrystal, take two admissible filtrations with G-conjugate defining cocharacters, realized by crystalline representations with their corresponding tensor data. The Q_p-torsor of tensor-preserving isomorphisms of the underlying representations has trivial class. This applies to the two p-divisible representations in Kisin17 Proposition1.1.19; it does not state that every G-torsor is trivial.
proofSteps: Use weakly-admissible implies admissible and the Wintenberger torsor-class formula: its class is determined by the fixed isocrystal and the cocharacter coinvariant. Conjugate filtrations give the same class, so their relative isomorphism torsor is neutral. The often cited Corollary4.5.3 is the unnumbered corollary following Proposition4.5.3. To use Wintenberger’s algebraically closed residue setup, restrict the two crystalline representations to a compatible complete extension with algebraically closed residue: their underlying Q_p tensor fibre functors, hence the isomorphism torsor, are unchanged.
acceptance: Prove the stated comparison with all displayed base rings and conventions; expose the actual maps, not only an existence proposition.

sources.match: The torsor-class formula and following corollary compare admissible filtered fibre functors. For conjugate filtrations their classes agree, so the relative rational torsor is neutral; this does not give an integral frame.

nodes.title: Specialization of a tensor-compatible Tate lattice
nodes.statement: For an adapted H/O_K with k=F̄_p and a fixed tensor W-frame, let g∈G(Q_p). Let L=Hom_Zp(T_pH,Z_p), with G acting on L. After a finite extension making gL Galois-stable, form the isogenous p-divisible group with dual Tate lattice gL (its Tate lattice is (gL)∨), form its Breuil–Kisin lattice, and reduce at u=0. The inverse notation on Tate modules is interpreted via this dual action. This gives g₀G(W)∈G(W[1/p])/G(W), depending only on gG(Z_p). Changing the initial W-frame changes the map by left multiplication by G(W). The output is a rational-lattice coset; g₀ is not required to lie in G(W).
proofSteps: An open stabilizer of the finite-index lattice gives the finite field extension. Apply the existing integral classification and tensor frame, then specialize its matrix. Show independence from further extensions and from right multiplication by G(Z_p).

nodes.title: An admissible filtration produces an adapted isogenous lift
